title: RemoteEvent
summary: One-way client ↔ server messaging. Fire-and-forget: FireServer sends to the server, FireClient/FireAllClients send to players, OnServerEvent/OnClientEvent receive. Reliable and ordered, but no return values.

verification.notes: Roblox's networking docs have shifted over the years toward recommending RemoteFunction only for true request/response and remotes for events; core RemoteEvent API has been stable.

methods.name: FireServer
methods.description: Client only. Sends a message to the server with any serializable arguments.

methods.name: FireClient
methods.description: Server only. Sends a message to one specific player.

methods.name: FireAllClients
methods.description: Server only. Broadcasts a message to every connected player.

events.name: OnServerEvent
events.description: Server only. Fires when any client calls FireServer. The firing Player is ALWAYS the first parameter — supplied by Roblox, and impossible for clients to fake.

events.name: OnClientEvent
events.description: Client only. Fires when the server calls FireClient/FireAllClients targeting this client. No player parameter here.

details.heading: Delivery guarantees
details.body: RemoteEvent is **reliable and ordered**: messages arrive in the order they were sent, and Roblox retransmits lost packets. It is still one-way — the sender gets no confirmation that the receiver handled the message (only that transport delivered it). If you need a reply, use RemoteFunction.

details.heading: Argument serialization
details.body: Arguments are serialized when sent: tables are deep-copied, Instances are passed as references (the other side must be able to access them), and metatables/functions/threads are not allowed. Total argument size is limited (historically ~65,536 bytes per message).

details.heading: Security
details.body: The first parameter of OnServerEvent (the Player) is injected by the engine and cannot be spoofed. Everything ELSE in the arguments is client-controlled and must be validated server-side. Never trust client-sent values for authoritative state.

explanation.whatItIs: A two-way intercom between clients and the server. Clients shout 'I pressed the button!' to the server; the server shouts 'the round started!' to clients. Messages are guaranteed to arrive, in order — but nobody sends a reply back through this intercom.
explanation.whyItExists: Client code and server code run in separate worlds with separate data. Remotes are the *only* way they talk, and RemoteEvent is the workhorse for everything that isn't a question-and-answer.
whenToUse: Client → server: input and intent ('buy this item', 'open this door', 'I'm equipping this tool')
Server → client(s): state updates and notifications ('round starting', 'your coins changed', 'play this sound')
Any message where you don't need an immediate answer
whenNotToUse: When you need a return value / synchronous answer — use RemoteFunction (sparingly)
For very frequent, loss-tolerant updates (position telemetry, cosmetic effects) — UnreliableRemoteEvent is cheaper
Between two scripts on the SAME side — use BindableEvent or just call the function/module directly
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
CLIENT                          SERVER
  │                               │
  │  RemoteEvent:FireServer(...)  │
  ├──────────────────────────────▶│
  │                               │ OnServerEvent(player, ...)
  │                               │    (player = who fired, always first)
  │                               │
  │  RemoteEvent:FireClient(plr)  │
  │◀──────────────────────────────┤
  │ OnClientEvent(...)            │
  │                               │
```
tips: Put RemoteEvents in ReplicatedStorage so both sides can reach them; use WaitForChild on the client
Always validate arguments on the server: type-check, range-check, and rate-limit
Use ONE remote with a command-string first argument ("buy", "equip") rather than dozens of remotes — dispatch with a handlers table
Remember the player parameter: server handlers get (player, arg1, arg2...) — the client never sends itself
commonMistakes: Listening on the wrong side: OnServerEvent only works in Scripts (server); OnClientEvent only in LocalScripts (client)
Forgetting that OnServerEvent's first parameter is the Player — arguments are shifted one to the right
Trusting client arguments: a client can send any number, string, or table — the server must validate
Firing before the other side has connected its handler — the message is lost; connect handlers early at startup
Expecting a reply from FireServer — RemoteEvent is one-way; nothing comes back unless the server fires separately

examples.title: Client → Server: request to purchase
examples.description: A LocalScript fires the intent; a Script validates and applies it.
examples.code:
-- == LocalScript (in a TextButton) ==
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local buyEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BuyItem")

script.Parent.Activated:Connect(function()
    buyEvent:FireServer("Sword")   -- client says WHAT it wants
end)

-- == Script (ServerScriptService) ==
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local buyEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BuyItem")
local PRICES = { Sword = 100, Shield = 50 }

buyEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemName)
    -- 1) VALIDATE: never trust the client
    if typeof(itemName) ~= "string" then return end
    local price = PRICES[itemName]
    if not price then return end

    -- 2) apply authoritatively on the server
    print(player.Name .. " bought " .. itemName .. " for " .. price)
end)
examples.whyItWorks: Roblox supplies `player` as the first OnServerEvent parameter — the server always knows WHO fired, and that identity can't be faked. The server still validates the itemName argument.
examples.commonMistake: Beginners often write `FireServer(player, "Sword")` trying to send the player themselves. Don't — the engine adds the player automatically.

examples.title: Server → Client: broadcast round start
examples.code:
-- == Script (server) ==
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local roundEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("RoundUpdate")

roundEvent:FireAllClients("RoundStart", 120)   -- message + seconds

-- == LocalScript (StarterGui) ==
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local roundEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("RoundUpdate")

roundEvent.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(message, seconds)
    if message == "RoundStart" then
        print("Round starts! Time:", seconds)
    end
end)
examples.whyItWorks: FireAllClients reaches every player at once. OnClientEvent receives exactly the arguments the server sent — no player parameter on the client side.

examples.title: One remote, many commands (dispatch pattern)
examples.code:
-- Server: one handler table beats 20 remotes
local handlers = {
    Buy   = function(player, item) print("buy", item) end,
    Equip = function(player, item) print("equip", item) end,
    Sell  = function(player, item) print("sell", item) end,
}

remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, command, ...)
    local fn = handlers[command]
    if fn then fn(player, ...) end   -- unknown commands ignored
end)

-- Client:
-- remote:FireServer("Buy", "Sword")
